criteria_results.criterion_text: Tapping it calls `identity.signOut()` and then `routeToSignIn(...)`, clearing the navigation stack and landing on `SignInScreen`
criteria_results.evidence: The _signOut() method (lines 182-186 of home_screen.dart) calls await widget.identity.signOut() followed by routeToSignIn(...). The test 'AC-002, AC-003: Tapping sign-out calls identity.signOut() and routes to SignInScreen' verifies the navigation behavior and that HomeScreen is removed from the tree (stack cleared).

criteria_results.criterion_text: After sign-out `identity.currentPrincipal` is `null` and the sign-in screen is shown (serves "Signing out clears the session and returns to the sign-in screen")
criteria_results.evidence: FakeIdentityProvider.signOut() sets _current to null (line 50 of fake_identity_provider.dart). Tests verify currentPrincipal is null after sign-out and SignInScreen is displayed. The BDD scenario test '@key-example @smoke' explicitly validates the complete flow.

criteria_results.criterion_text: The affordance is driven through the `IdentityProvider` port — the widget test uses `FakeIdentityProvider`, no Keycloak adapter required
criteria_results.evidence: All tests use FakeIdentityProvider (setUp at line 20-24 of sign_out_test.dart). The test 'AC-004: Sign-out is driven through IdentityProvider port' explicitly validates that the port abstraction works without any Keycloak dependency. The implementation only calls the port method widget.identity.signOut().

criteria_results.evidence: The test suite in sign_out_test.dart contains no assertions about background refresh behavior or race conditions. All tests focus only on the UI affordance and the port-level signOut() contract. No mocking or verification of adapter-internal refresh mechanisms.
